entries.text: Inflation is when your money buys less, because prices across the economy are rising.
The US tracks this with the Consumer Price Index, a basket of goods the average household actually buys.
When demand outpaces supply, buyers bid prices up. That is demand-pull inflation.
When a key input gets scarce, oil, labor, chips, producers pass the cost along. That is cost-push.
And once everyone expects prices to rise, workers demand higher wages, which raises prices again. That is the built-in spiral.
The Federal Reserve fights all three by raising interest rates, cooling demand, and breaking the cycle.
